nodes.name: Graphene Oxide Nanoribbons Preparation
nodes.procedure: 8 g of C-grade MWCNT (NTL) was added into a mixture of 1000 mL of sulfuric acid (Carlo Erba, 96%) and 110 mL of phosphoric acid (Merck, 85%) and stirred. Over the next 4 days, 8 wt equivalents of KMnO4 (8×8 g) was added to the mixture under stirring. The mixture was then quenched with ice, followed by adding 30% H2O2 until the color was changed from purple to yellowish. The supernatant was discarded, a portion of ultrapure water was added, and the mixture was centrifuged for 30 min at 10500 rpm. The obtained solid was redispersed in 5% HCl for 2 h to eliminate any residual metals. Afterward, the mixture was centrifuged for 30 min at 10500 rpm, followed by supernatant decantation. The last cleaning step involved redispersing the GONR in ultrapure water and soaking until the next day, followed by centrifugation at 10500 rpm for 1 h. Five washing cycles in ultrapure water were conducted. Nanoribbons were redispersed in ultrapure water (~20 g L⁻¹) and sonicated for 15 min to exfoliate. The suspension was freeze-dried.

nodes.name: TiO2 Coating on Dried GONR
nodes.procedure: 0.1 g of dried GONR was mixed with 1 mL of propanol solution containing 0.5 mmol of Ti isopropoxide (97%). After mixing at room temperature, Ti isopropoxide was hydrolyzed by adding 0.2 mL of Milli-Q water. The obtained mixture was dried in air at 50°C.
nodes.source_text: In the next step, TiO2 coating on GONR was prepared. For this purpose, 0.1 g of dried GONR was mixed with 1 mL of propanol (Honeywell, 99.8% solution containing 0.5 mmol of Ti isopropoxide (Aldrich, 97%)). After mixing at room temperature, Ti isopropoxide was hydrolyzed by adding 0.2 mL of water... dried in air at 50°C.

nodes.name: Pt Deposition and TiONx Formation
nodes.procedure: Water solution containing 35 mg of Pt(NH3)4(NO3)2 (1 mL) was added to the TiO2-coated GONR and lightly milled in mortar at 50°C until evaporation. The mixture was then thermally treated in 90% NH3/9.5% Ar/0.5% H2 atmosphere: heated at 2°C/min to 250°C for 2 h, then at 10°C/min to 730°C for 3 h, then cooled at 10°C/min to room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiONx XRD shows TiONx peaks at 37.1° and 43.1° (00-049-1325) and Pt (111) at 39.8°, (200) at 46.3° (04-0802); no TiO2 peaks (01-073-8760); Pt/C shows Pt peaks indicating slightly smaller particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD pattern of the base TiONx support (black line, Figure 1a) contains diffraction peaks at 37.1 and 43.1° originating from the TiONx crystal structure (00-049-1325), while the reflections related to the initial TiO2 compound (01-073-8760) are absent ... In the case of Pt/TiONx, the same TiONx-related peaks are present ... peaks appearing at 39.8 and 46.3° correspond to 111 and 200 reflections of Pt (JCPDS card 04-0802)

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiONx STEM shows Pt NPs (2-3 nm, <5 nm total) predominantly anchored to TiONx flakes (~20 nm) on graphene nanoribbons (~150 nm width); Pt/C shows ~2 nm particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Close inspection of the higher-magnification scanning TEM (STEM) image (Figure 1c) reveals that Pt particles are indeed almost exclusively grafted on TiONx ... Analysis of particle size distribution (PSD) in Pt/TiONx (Figure 1d) shows that the Pt particles are generally below 5 nm in diameter, the majority being between 2 and 3 nm
